examples: Rain can damage a book.
Do not damage the plants.
The dog damaged my shoe.

more.def: To harm something so that it is broken or works less well.
examples: The storm damaged the roof of the barn.
Too much sun can damage your skin.
Hail damaged the cars parked on the street.
It is dangerous to play near the road.
A hot stove is dangerous.
That dog is not dangerous.

more.def: Likely to cause harm or injury.
examples: Swimming in the river is dangerous when the water is high.
It is dangerous to ride a bike without a helmet.
Some wild mushrooms are dangerous to eat.

easy.def: To pick what you will do.
examples: I can't decide which game to play.
I decided to wear my red hat.
You decide what we eat for lunch.

more.def: To make a choice after thinking about it.
examples: We decided to walk to school instead of taking the bus.
The judges will decide who wins the art contest.
He could not decide between the puppy and the kitten.
Be gentle. The butterfly has delicate wings.
The glass cup is delicate.
A spider web is delicate.

more.def: Easily broken or damaged, so it needs gentle care.
examples: The delicate glass ornament was wrapped in soft paper.
The delicate flower petals fell off in the wind.
Fixing a watch is delicate work that takes steady hands.
This apple pie is delicious.
Grandma makes delicious soup.
The ripe berries are delicious.

more.def: Very pleasant to taste or smell.
examples: A delicious smell of fresh bread came from the kitchen.
We shared a delicious meal at the new restaurant.
The mango was so delicious that I asked for another.
Baby birds depend on their mother for food.
I depend on my dad to drive me to school.
Our plans depend on the weather.

more.def: To need or trust someone or something for help or support.
examples: Plants depend on sunlight and water to grow.
Many people depend on buses to get to work.
Whether we win depends on how well we work together.

easy.def: To tell what something is like.
examples: Describe your dog. Is he big or small?
Describe what you see out the window.
He described his new house to me.

more.def: To use words to tell what someone or something is like.
examples: She described the storm so well that we could almost hear the thunder.
The witness described the car to the police.
Can you describe how the soup tastes?

easy.def: A very dry place with lots of sand and not much rain.
examples: Camels live in the desert.
It is hot in the desert in the day.
A snake slid across the desert.

more.def: A very dry area of land that gets little rain and has few plants.
examples: Only tough plants like cactuses can grow in the desert.
Deserts can be very hot in the day and cold at night.
The travelers crossed the desert on camels.
My socks are different colors.
We go to different schools.
This apple tastes different.

more.def: Not like something or someone else.
examples: The twins look alike, but they have very different hobbies.
People in different countries celebrate the new year in different ways.
My handwriting looks different when I use a pen.

easy.def: To go away so you can't see it.
examples: The sun will disappear behind the clouds.
My socks always disappear!
The rabbit disappeared into a hole.

more.def: To go out of sight or stop existing.
examples: The snow disappeared as soon as the weather warmed up.
The plane disappeared into the clouds.
The stain disappeared after we washed the shirt.

easy.def: To make someone sad because something did not happen.
examples: I do not want to disappoint my team.
The rain disappointed the kids.
I will try not to disappoint you.

more.def: To make someone unhappy by not doing what they hoped for or expected.
examples: The canceled trip disappointed the whole class.
The movie's ending disappointed many fans.
She did not want to disappoint her coach by quitting.

easy.def: To find something for the first time.
examples: I discovered a tiny shell in the sand.
We discovered a nest in the tree.
He discovered he likes peas.

more.def: To find or learn something that you did not know about before.
examples: Scientists discovered a new kind of frog in the rainforest.
The hikers discovered a hidden waterfall.
I discovered that I am good at chess.

easy.def: How far it is from one place to another.
examples: The distance to school is short.
We can see the hills in the distance.
I can throw the ball a long distance.

more.def: The amount of space between two places or things.
examples: The distance between our town and the ocean is two hundred miles.
The runners trained to race a distance of five miles.
From a distance, the two houses look exactly the same.

easy.def: A long time with no rain.
examples: The plants died in the drought.
The pond dried up in the drought.
There was no water to spare in the drought.

more.def: A long period with little or no rain, so the land becomes very dry.
examples: During the drought, the farmers' fields turned brown.
After the long drought, the river was only a trickle.
The town asked people to save water during the drought.
